lastCommit.message:
OTA-1877 — the hunt reads its last beat

A hunt can now carry an authored trailing `checkKind: null` beat behind its
final boss, and the player will actually read it. ENGINE SUPPORT ONLY — not one
line of hunt prose is written here, and no hunt data file has a diff.

NOTHING SHIPPED CHANGES, AND THE SUITE PINS WHY. All 18 hunts end ON their final
boss (13 standard_7 at index 6, 5 bait_switch_5 at index 4) and zero carry a
trailing beat, so `lastBoss + 1` and `stages.length` are the same number for
every one of them and the new loop body never runs. This is a capability, not a
fix to live content.

THE DEFECT WAS PROVEN THROUGH THE REAL DEFEAT PATH, not by calling a helper.
`advanceHunt` has consumed AND READ OUT trailing null stages since OTA-1219, but
the final boss FREEZES for the kill (OTA-796), so the last stage never reaches
`advanceHunt`. The defeat credit is the only way out of it, and it wrote
`stage: stages.length` outright. On a fixture shaped boss -> beat, a real
`resolveEnemyDefeat` measured stage 0 -> 2 with the beat NEVER logged, the hunt
turn-in-eligible immediately, and the skip surviving a persist. There was no
recovery path afterwards: the stage that would have read the beat is already
behind the record.

ONE SEMANTIC OWNER, NOT A SECOND COPY. `readOutTrailingHuntBeats` is OTA-1219's
loop extracted into `questSlice`; `advanceHunt` delegates to it from
`record.stage + 1` and the defeat credit calls it from the FINAL BOSS INDEX + 1.
It is deliberately NOT `nextActionableStage`, which computes an index and
knows nothing about the log — the contract is that the beat is READ OUT exactly
once, so the owner has to be the thing that both advances and narrates. That
helper's own header (OTA-1583) named this class already and repaired the escort
clear; this is the sibling kill path left behind.

THE BOUNDARY IS CROSSED ONCE, AND BOTH EDGES ARE LOAD-BEARING. `rec.stage >=
lastBoss` becomes the window `>= lastBoss && <= lastBoss + 1`. The old open form
was harmless while the credit only rewrote `stages.length` over itself — a second
kill of a respawned target re-logged the close line and nothing else — but a
credit that READS a beat would read it again, hence the new upper edge. The lower
edge is OTA-426's rule kept exactly: several hunts carry a MID-hunt boss stage
that spawns the same scaled target, and killing it there must not complete the
hunt and skip the back half. Narrowing to `=== lastBoss` was tried and was WRONG
— caught by OTA-426's own suite, which says so in as many words: `advanceHunt(6)
lands the record at stage 7`. So the guard reasons from progression rather than
from whether an epilogue exists: with no trailing beat a re-kill still only
re-logs a line, and consuming a beat puts the record PAST the window so it can
never be read twice.

NO ECONOMY CHANGE, and the forensics are why rather than the intent. The kill
pays nothing — it logs "return to a posting agent"; `turnInHunt` pays, gated on
`if (record.stage < candidate.stages.length) refuse`. So `stage` is the turn-in
ELIGIBILITY gate and the bounty is the turn-in's alone. Measured at the kill on
a 780-bounty fixture: TC 100 -> 110, which is ordinary spoils, not the bounty.
`turnInHunt` is untouched, as are rewards, spawns, enemy stats, travel, native
code, DISPLAY_VERSION and runtimeVersion.

PERSISTENCE, STATED EXACTLY AND NOT ONE WORD FURTHER. The walked stage lives on
`player.activeHunts`, which is in the save payload — the field the turn-in gate
reads and the field that stops the boundary being re-credited. What the test
proves is narrower: the record still carries the walked stage across a
`persist()` call, which is not a storage round-trip. NARRATION PERSISTENCE IS NOT
CLAIMED — `gameLog` appears zero times in the save system, so a read-out beat is
transient by construction. That is the existing contract; this change neither
alters it nor pretends otherwise.

THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS, none committed. NC1 (restore the jump AND remove the
read-out call) 4 red including the one-beat case — the first attempt replaced
only the written stage, left the call in place, and went 1 red, which is exactly
why the control had to remove the call. NC2 (guard open again) red on the
duplicate case. NC3 (arithmetic correct, narration removed) 4 red — the proof
that this suite tests READ-OUT and not index maths.

                                   shipped shape unchanged, duplicate defeat
                                   inert, two beats in order, stop at the first
                                   actionable stage, no bogus travel armed,
                                   bounty not paid at the kill, progression
                                   survives a persist

The new suite's player fixture spreads OTA-1484's `placedAt` rather than writing
a bare `currentLocationId`, so the shrink-only ratchet holds at 54 and the
"ground does not move" assertion is measuring the engine and not a lucky frame.

NOT CLAIMED. The 18 hunt ending texts are a separate content package and are not
begun here. No physical-device verification.
